verdict: Delta's revenue hit a September-quarter record of $20.2B, up 21%, but a 69% jump in fuel costs cut operating income to $1.5B and net income fell to $756M from $1.4B a year ago.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Total operating revenue was a September-quarter record $20.2B, vs $16.7B a year ago; excluding the refinery's third-party sales, adjusted revenue rose 16% to $17.6B

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $2.17 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $1.72, mainly excluding mark-to-market losses on equity investments

kpis.label: Aircraft fuel cost
kpis.note: Aircraft fuel and related taxes of $4,351M, up 69% from $2,570M a year ago — the main reason profit fell despite record revenue

kpis.label: Passenger revenue
kpis.note: Up 15% vs a year ago on flat capacity, with premium products growing 18%; cargo revenue rose 29% to $301M

segments.name: Passenger
segments.note: Tickets and travel-related fees — Delta's core business, about 77% of revenue. Up 15% on flat capacity, as higher fares (yields) and fuller planes offset no growth in seats; premium-cabin revenue grew 18%.

segments.name: Cargo
segments.note: Freight and mail carried in the bellies of passenger planes. Up 29%, split roughly evenly between more volume and higher prices.

segments.name: Other
segments.note: Everything else: the Monroe oil refinery's sales to third parties ($2,601M), loyalty-program revenue from partners such as credit-card issuers, and maintenance (MRO) work sold to other airlines. Up 48%, mostly because refinery sales rose with fuel prices.

opex.name: Salaries and related costs
opex.note: Pay and benefits for Delta's employees — its largest single cost. Up 9% vs a year ago.

opex.name: Passenger commissions and other selling expenses
opex.note: Commissions and the cost of selling tickets, including card fees. Shown as selling expenses.

opex.name: Profit sharing
opex.note: The share of profits paid out to employees under Delta's profit-sharing plan.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: The cost of aircraft, engines and equipment wearing out over time.

opex.name: Passenger service
opex.note: Looking after passengers — food, drinks, in-flight entertainment and amenities.

opex.name: Other operating expenses
opex.note: All remaining operating costs not listed separately on the statement.

follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding. Cost of revenue groups the direct costs of flying and of the ancillary businesses — aircraft fuel and related taxes ($4,351M), ancillary businesses and refinery operating expense ($2,868M, combining the statement's refinery expense of $2,601M and MRO expense of $267M), contracted services ($1,277M), landing fees and other rents ($1,021M), aircraft maintenance materials and outside repairs ($662M) and regional carrier expense ($680M). Every other operating expense line is an operating expense in the chart, so each statement line sits in exactly one bucket.

takeaways.title: Record revenue on flat capacity
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 21% to a September-quarter record $20,186M. Passenger revenue grew 15% to $15,534M with no growth in seats — fuller planes and higher fares did the work — while cargo rose 29% and loyalty revenue grew 18%. Delta guided to roughly 20% revenue growth again in the December quarter.

takeaways.title: Fuel ate the growth
takeaways.text: Aircraft fuel and related taxes cost $4,351M, up 69% from $2,570M a year ago in one of the most elevated fuel environments in years. Operating income fell to $1,454M from $1,684M despite the record top line, and net income fell to $756M from $1,417M. Delta still expects full-year pre-tax profit of roughly $4.5B, absorbing about $6B of extra fuel costs this year.

takeaways.title: Adjusted profit held up better
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was $1.15, but excluding a $218M mark-to-market loss on equity investments and similar items, adjusted EPS was $1.72 and adjusted pre-tax income was $1.5B — matching last year. Delta guided to full-year EPS of $5.10–$5.60 and about $2.5B of free cash flow.

oneTimers: Non-operating results include a $218M mark-to-market loss on equity investments — paper losses on stakes Delta holds, which it excludes from adjusted earnings. That gap is most of the difference between GAAP EPS of $1.15 and adjusted EPS of $1.72.
otherDetail: Interest expense, net of $146M and a $218M loss on investments, plus $18M of miscellaneous costs, partly offset by a $2M gain on early repayment of debt — a net $380M cost below operating income.
footerNote: Flow adaptation: airlines report no gross-profit line; cost of revenue here groups the direct costs of flying (see the $100 note for the breakdown).
